evidence: checkpoint.lisp:249-254 `(if (= errno sb-posix:eexist) (fnn-refuse ...) (fnn-os-fail errno destination))`, and checkpoint.lisp:467-473 `(handler-case (progn (fnn-clone-publish-no-replace stage target) ...) (fnn-os-error () (fnn-indeterminate "clone directory publication is uncertain")))`.
fix: Classify renameat2's own errno as a refusal (nothing was published) and keep fnn-indeterminate for failures after the rename returned 0 (the parent fsync).
reviewer: Any errno other than EEXIST goes through fnn-os-fail (checkpoint.lisp:249-254), and the handler-case at checkpoint.lisp:467-473 maps every fnn-os-error, including a failed renameat2, to fnn-indeterminate. renameat2 is atomic, so EINVAL, ENOSYS or EXDEV means nothing was renamed. Only the parent fsync after a successful rename is genuinely uncertain. This misclassifies a definite refusal as uncertain, which AGENTS.md's 'uncertain, refused and accepted stay distinct' rule forbids.
scenario: On a filesystem that does not support RENAME_NOREPLACE, renameat2 fails with EINVAL before anything is renamed, which is a definite failure. It is still reported as 'publication is uncertain' (exit 3, a recovery event), so the operator is sent into recovery for a rename that certainly did not happen. Only an error from the fsync of the parent after a successful rename is genuinely uncertain.
title: Definite renameat2 failures (EINVAL/ENOSYS/EXDEV) are reported as an indeterminate publication
